questions.text: Why should a host keep separate argument buffers for interleaved streamed tool calls and wait for each call’s completion signal before parsing?

options.A: To sort all calls alphabetically before any executor can run.
options.B: To combine all argument fragments into one shared JSON object.
options.C: To avoid mixing different calls or parsing incomplete JSON.
options.D: To ensure every call finishes execution in its request order.

questions.explanation: Separate buffers preserve call identity, and completion signals prevent attempts to decode incomplete argument JSON.

questions.text: A create_record call returns the ID needed by update_record. How should the host schedule these two calls?

options.A: Run both concurrently and match their results by call ID.
options.B: Finish create_record, then supply its ID to update_record.
options.C: Start update_record first so it can wait for any new record.
options.D: Run both concurrently using the tool name as a shared key.

questions.explanation: The second call depends on the first call’s output. Correlation IDs do not remove this data dependency.

questions.text: A CallBuffer contains args_buf='{"city":"Tokyo"}' but done=False. What does its try_parse() method return?

options.A: The dictionary {"city": "Tokyo"}, because the JSON is complete.
options.B: A JSONDecodeError, because no call_stop event has arrived.
options.C: The unchanged string, because parsing has not been enabled.
options.D: None, because the done check occurs before json.loads.

questions.explanation: try_parse returns None immediately while done is False, even if args_buf happens to contain valid JSON.
